clue.text: Resident, before long, admitting hard worker, say

indicators.note: to admit is to let something in, so the phrase before it takes the next item inside itself

parts.note: 'in a bit' means shortly, before long
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
a worker ant is one kind of ant; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A long-standing resident who, it is hinted, has been taking in a hard-working lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before long' is a time phrase, not a place; H goes inside it near the front, and 'worker, say' is an insect, the worker caste of an ant colony.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant is someone who lives in a place, a straightforward synonym for a resident.

clue.text: It's more of a hand than a foot

definitions.text: It's more of a hand than a foot

parts.words: It's more of a hand than a foot
parts.note: surface reading: something that is more like a hand than a foot, as if comparing body parts
setter's reading: a hand is a horse-measuring unit of four of these small units, while a foot holds twelve, so this unit is a bigger share of a hand

explanation.walkthrough: Hand and foot are both units of length: a hand is four inches, a foot twelve, so an inch is a quarter of a hand but only a twelfth of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The inch is the imperial unit that forms a larger fraction of a hand measurement than of a foot measurement.

clue.text: Prince provided a cross for Northern town

parts.note: Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare
'provided' and 'if' both introduce a condition
taken as written
a cross is drawn as an X

explanation.surface: A royal visitor brought a cross along for a town in the North.
explanation.walkthrough: Halifax is a town in West Yorkshire, in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Halifax is a Yorkshire mill town, so it is an example of a town in the north of England.

clue.text: In clubs, assess differently where some high-fliers sit

indicators.note: doing something differently means arranging it another way, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Members of clubs are asked to judge things in a new way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-fliers' is both successful executives and people literally flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Business class is the premium section of an aircraft cabin, where executives and other successful travellers are seated.

clue.text: Island in East that is oddly lacking in colour

indicators.note: oddly here means taking only the letters in odd-numbered positions of the words before it

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of these two words
wan means pale, short of colour

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the East is oddly drab and colourless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in East' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay: the island lies off East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is a large island off the coast of China, so it is an island in the Far East.

clue.text: Anaesthetised English left-winger came to

parts.note: an anaesthetic leaves the body numb
E is the abbreviation for English
a Red is a left-wing radical

explanation.surface: A sedated English socialist woke up after surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came to' looks like regaining consciousness after anaesthetic; here it means totalled, as in 'the bill came to ten pounds'.
explanation.definitionFit: To number is to amount to a total, so 'numbered' and 'came to' both mean added up to.

clue.text: Within academic education, reduced number of degrees

indicators.note: within tells the solver the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of academic and the start of education

explanation.surface: Cutting back the number of degrees awarded in higher education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degrees' looks academic but means temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iced has been chilled, so its temperature, measured in degrees, has been lowered.

clue.text: Low mark in French I called wrong

indicators.note: something called wrong has been put out of its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A student admits getting a poor grade in French for a wrong answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low mark' is not a poor grade but a mark written below a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedilla is the hook placed beneath a c in French, a diacritic that sits low on the letter.

clue.text: American bowler's to take on cricket team here

parts.note: in America a bowler hat is called a derby
the possessive ending taken as written
to take on staff is to hire them

explanation.surface: A US bowler is signing up with an English county side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket but is the hat. Derbyshire is an English county with a first-class cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: Derbyshire is the county that is home to Derbyshire County Cricket Club, so a cricket team plays there.

clue.text: Conservative is alone backing powerful organisations

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: going backwards means the words before it are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
solo means on one's own

explanation.surface: A lone Tory politician is supporting big corporations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for organisations; it reverses IS SOLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi, plural of colossus, are giants, a figurative word for huge and dominant bodies.

clue.text: Follow a random path as repairman covering area

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: a mender fixes things
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A repairman wanders aimlessly around the area he covers on his rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander along a winding, aimless course, like the bends of a river.

clue.text: Father of Asian maltreated, in a way

indicators.note: treated badly suggests being knocked about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An Asian man's father was treated badly, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean to some extent or in a rough, imperfect manner, as in 'he can cook, after a fashion'.

clue.text: In essence, provide resources for article, using brain

parts.note: to fund is to supply money for
a is the indefinite article
doing something mentally means with the mind

explanation.surface: Basically, a journalist is being paid to write a piece that needs some thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentally means at root or at bottom, which is what 'in essence' says.

clue.text: Aids sector wrongly excluded from society

indicators.note: something done wrongly is out of order, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: People in the AIDS charity sector were unfairly shunned by the community.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise is to shun or banish someone from a group, as Athenians did by vote.

clue.text: Are joining Society that's nicer to fellows?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
'we are' in the sense 'we exist'

explanation.surface: A question about whether a club is friendlier to its fellows than to others.
explanation.walkthrough: The S comes first, with EXIST joined after it. The definition is playful: a sexist treats one sex, here fellows, better than the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexist favours one sex, so someone kinder to men than to women fits the description.

clue.text: Achieve without expert's approval? Just the opposite

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word stands around the other

parts.note: to reach a goal is to achieve it
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: Getting results with no expert's sign-off is, in fact, criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside. The ''s' is 'is', joining wordplay to definition, and 'Just the opposite' turns approval into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproach is blame or disapproval, the reverse of approval.

clue.text: Key ceremony and broadcast raised standards

parts.note: C is a musical key
a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An important ceremony was televised and standards went up.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the standards or tests by which something is judged.

clue.text: Doing very little to improve one's health?

definitions.text: Doing very little to improve one's health?

parts.words: Doing very little to improve one's health?
parts.note: surface reading: a lazy person making little effort to get fit
setter's reading: inactivity is itself the treatment, a prescribed period of lying still to recover

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a reproach for idleness; in fact idleness is the medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest cure is a medical regime of bed rest and inactivity prescribed to restore health.

clue.text: Event seen in evening paper saddened

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
feeling down means feeling sad

explanation.surface: Something reported in the evening newspaper left readers upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening paper' looks like one phrase but splits: 'evening' ends the definition, 'paper' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundown is sunset, the daily occurrence that marks the coming of evening.

clue.text: Fling a fellow's had with blonde

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow
fair hair is blonde

explanation.surface: A man has had a brief romance with a blonde.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a short romantic relationship, which is what a fling is.

clue.text: Reduce severity of clot you reported, over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit on top of the next

parts.note: a clot is a fool, an ass

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word before it is taken by its sound

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A doctor tries to ease a blood clot you described, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clot' suggests a blood clot but is a British word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage pain or grief is to ease it, making it less severe.

clue.text: Harden or soften

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to toughen steel by heating and cooling it
second meaning: to moderate or tone down

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions look like opposites, which is the joke: the same verb does both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Metalworkers temper steel to toughen it, while to temper criticism is to make it milder.

clue.text: Visual aids placed just in front of pupils

definitions.text: Visual aids placed just in front of pupils

parts.words: Visual aids placed just in front of pupils
parts.note: surface reading: a teacher's charts and slides set up before a class of schoolchildren
setter's reading: the pupils are the dark centres of the eyes, and the aids sit directly on the eye over them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Visual aids' and 'pupils' paint a classroom; both are about eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: These thin corrective lenses rest on the surface of the eye, right over the pupil, to improve sight.

clue.text: Without a break, attend strike

indicators.note: with no gap between them, the two words of the phrase that follows are run together as one

parts.note: to attend an event is to be present there; the two-word phrase meaning that is written with no space

explanation.surface: Workers are told to keep turning up continuously, and to go on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a break' tells you to close up the space in BE AT, attending being 'being at' something.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat is to hit repeatedly, so it is a synonym of strike.

clue.text: Provide backing for track about pair holding hands

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: spoor is the track or trail of an animal
in bridge, North and South are partners who each hold a hand of cards

explanation.surface: Financing a running track for a couple who walk hand in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding hands' looks romantic; in bridge each player holds a hand of cards, and North and South play as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor gives financial support, which is to provide backing for something.

clue.text: Pawn and rook I win, playing chess — or bishop, perhaps

parts.note: P is the chess notation for pawn
R is the chess notation for rook
taken as written
checkmate wins a game of chess

explanation.surface: A chess player lists pieces: a pawn, a rook, or a bishop to deliver victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop' looks like another chess piece, but it is the churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is the chief archbishop of a country, so a senior bishop is an example.

clue.text: Finishes off crossword puzzle on Sunday for contest

indicators.note: the finish of each word is its final letter, so only the ends are kept

parts.note: final letter
final letter
final letter
final letter

explanation.surface: A solver completes the Sunday crossword in time for a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contest' looks like a noun for a competition; as a verb it means dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest a claim is to challenge it, and to deny it is to reject it as untrue.

clue.text: It's hot in a fire, then — possibly as indicated by this?

definitions.text: It's hot in a fire, then — possibly as indicated by this?

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters may be put together another way

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Things get hot in a fire, as a thermometer would show.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes in among the letters of 'a fire, then', and the lot is rearranged. Read whole, the clue describes the scale that measures that heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fahrenheit is a temperature scale, so the heat of a fire could be shown in its degrees.
